"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

input.quote: 8. COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding us. Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "staff" return only the unsolicited-email section (§ 7), access-restriction and indemnity references to "employees", and no restrictive covenant on hiring. Full review of the two likely locations — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client, p0050–p0058) and § 10 (Confidentiality, p0061–p0068) — confirms no employee non-solicit. The only reference to a restrictive covenant is the cross-reference in § 8(d) (p0054) to a separate "Non-Competition Agreement", and that reference is limited to the scope of TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, not to hiring of personnel; that separate document is outside this review. This matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so no redline is required.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The Agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us:

- **Text searches** for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "staff" surfaced only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), the access-restriction covenant in § 8(c), and incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities.
- **Full read of the two likely locations** flagged by the plan — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirms no hiring restriction is tucked into our covenants or the confidentiality obligations.
- **One cross-reference noted:** § 8(d) (p0054) refers to a separate "Non-Competition Agreement", but only to bound TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data — not personnel hiring. That instrument sits outside this document; if it is in the deal package, it is worth a separate check for a non-solicit binding us.

This is our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so we take no action rather than importing the mutual fallback.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.summary: Expand TrueLink's indemnity in Section 12.b to cover third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Interface and services, TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client data, and TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and add a standard indemnity procedure.
input.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity currently covers only its own breach of the Agreement, so we would carry the risk of third-party claims that the Interface or hosted services infringe IP rights, while our own indemnity is very broad. We added IP infringement, violation of law, TrueLink-caused data compromise and gross negligence/willful misconduct, plus a standard notice-and-control procedure; if TrueLink prefers, we can accept the IP indemnity with customary exclusions (our modifications, combinations and specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no competitive restraint on Mortgage Logic.com:

- **Section 2(a) (p0022/p0024)** works in our favour: it expressly confirms we are "not obligated to utilize the License and [are] free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system... to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink," subject only to non-infringement of TrueLink IP and our confidentiality obligations. That is better than the playbook's preferred position.
- The licence-scope language ("in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables") limits how we may use TrueLink's Interface, not what business we may operate — so it is not a field-of-use restraint on us.
- **Section 8 (Client covenants)** is confined to legal compliance, access control, non-misrepresentation of underwriting decisions, and content warranties.
- The single "Non-Competition Agreement" reference in **Section 8(d) (p0054)** limits *TrueLink's* licence to use Credit Data — a restraint on the vendor, which is acceptable to us.

One diligence flag for the deal team (not a redline): the "Non-Competition Agreement" is referenced but not defined or attached here. We should review that document separately to confirm it does not impose any covenant on us, since a restraint located there would fall outside this agreement's protections.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds us. Section 2(a) affirmatively confirms that Client is free to acquire, develop, license or use competing software and services (subject only to non-infringement of TrueLink IP and confidentiality), which exceeds the playbook's preferred position. The Client covenants in Section 8 are limited to legal compliance, access control, non-misrepresentation of underwriting decisions and content warranties — none restrict the businesses we may operate or products we may buy or build. The only "Non-Competition Agreement" reference (Section 8(d)) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, i.e., a restraint on the vendor, which is acceptable. The licence-scope wording in Section 2(a) ("in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables") limits permitted use of TrueLink's Interface rather than our business activities, so it is not a field-of-use restraint on us. No redline required; separately, diligence on the referenced Non-Competition Agreement is advisable since it is not defined here.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.quote: 8. COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding us. Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "staff" return only the unsolicited-email section (§ 7), access-restriction and indemnity references to "employees", and no restrictive covenant on hiring. Full review of the two likely locations — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client, p0050–p0058) and § 10 (Confidentiality, p0061–p0068) — confirms no employee non-solicit. The only reference to a restrictive covenant is the cross-reference in § 8(d) (p0054) to a separate "Non-Competition Agreement", and that reference is limited to the scope of TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, not to hiring of personnel; that separate document is outside this review. This matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so no redline is required.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The Agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us:

- **Text searches** for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "staff" surfaced only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), the access-restriction covenant in § 8(c), and incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities.
- **Full read of the two likely locations** flagged by the plan — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirms no hiring restriction is tucked into our covenants or the confidentiality obligations.
- **One cross-reference noted:** § 8(d) (p0054) refers to a separate "Non-Competition Agreement", but only to bound TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data — not personnel hiring. That instrument sits outside this document; if it is in the deal package, it is worth a separate check for a non-solicit binding us.

This is our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so we take no action rather than importing the mutual fallback.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

input.quote: claim arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder.
input.rationale: Section 12.b gives us a TrueLink indemnity, but it is limited to TrueLink's breach of the Agreement or failure to perform. It contains no indemnity for third-party claims that the Interface or the hosted/support services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property, nor for TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content/Credit Data, or TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. By contrast, our indemnity in 12.a is very broad (any breach, all Web Site/Client Content claims expressly "without regard to any knowledge limitation," and product-liability claims for anything transmitted from the Web Site), and Section 8.e only gives an actual-knowledge non-infringement warranty on Client Content — so nothing shifts IP risk in TrueLink's own technology to TrueLink. The agreement also lacks any indemnity procedure (notice, control of defense, consent to settlement, cooperation). Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, restrictive covenants).**

- **What we found:** No general "sole supplier" clause, but § 3(i) (p0042) contains a hidden requirements obligation — "Client **shall order** TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface." That is a de facto sole-source commitment for credit reports, with no category/term limit and no performance-based exit.
- **Not flagged:** the non-exclusive license grant in § 2(a), which actually helps us (we expressly stay free to acquire or develop competing software/services), and the nonexclusive license we grant TrueLink over Credit Data in § 8(d) (not exclusivity against us).
- **Redline (preferred, validated ok:true):** "shall order" → "may order from", plus a confirmation that nothing obligates us to obtain credit reports exclusively from TrueLink. The comment offers the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, auto-terminating on service-level failure) if TrueLink pushes back on volume.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 3(i) imposes a requirements-style sourcing obligation on us: we must order the credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no category/time limit and no exit for TrueLink's performance failures. Although the license in Section 2(a) is non-exclusive and expressly preserves our right to use alternative systems, that carve-out does not displace this mandatory per-borrower purchase obligation. The playbook preferred position is no sole-supplier obligation on the customer, so we make the order optional and confirm non-exclusivity; the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, terminable on service-level failure) is offered in the comment. The nonexclusive licenses granted to TrueLink in Section 8(d) are not exclusivity against us and are not flagged.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds us anywhere in this Agreement, which matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so no redline or comment is proposed. Regex and literal searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "no-hire", "poach", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel", "staff" and "leave the employ" return only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), the incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities, and § 8(c) (quoted), where "employees" appears solely in an access-restriction covenant and imposes no hiring restraint. Full reads of the two likely locations, § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client, p0050–p0058) and § 10 (Confidentiality, p0061–p0068), confirm the absence. The only restrictive-covenant reference is § 8(d) (p0054), whose cross-reference to the separate "Non-Competition Agreement" is scoped to the limitations on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, not to hiring of personnel. The failed deterministic checks (duration of 12 months or less; general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of there being no non-solicit clause to measure, not defects; the fallback (mutual 12-month non-solicit with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs) is unnecessary here. Reviewer note: the separate Non-Competition Agreement sits outside this document, so any hiring restriction living there is not captured by this finding and should be diligenced separately.

input.rationale: The only liability cap in the agreement (buried at the end of Section 12, Indemnity) is one-sided: it limits TrueLink's liability alone, leaving Client's liability — including its very broad indemnity under Section 12a — entirely uncapped, which is our walk-away position. The cap basis is also narrow ("total compensation paid" for Hosting and Support Services only, excluding other agreed services under Section 5a and amounts payable but unpaid), and there is no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and no carve-out set beyond TrueLink's gross negligence/wilful misconduct. The redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and places indemnification, confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, with Client's payment obligations not treated as capped damages.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual, set it at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made the limitation of liability mutual and meaningful — the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000 — rather than a one-way cap that protects only TrueLink while leaving Client's liability unlimited, and we added a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages. Consistent with our playbook, indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Client's obligation to pay fees is not capped; if helpful we can fall back to a straight twelve months' fees cap with these carve-outs retained.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN, critical).**

What I found:
- **§12.b (p0073/p0075)** does contain a TrueLink indemnity, but it is confined to TrueLink's *breach of the Agreement or failure to perform*. There is **no IP infringement indemnity** for the Interface/Hosting/Support Services, and nothing for TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused data compromise, or gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- **§12.a (p0071/p0072)** by contrast imposes a very broad Client indemnity — any Client breach, all Web Site/Client Content claims "without regard to any knowledge limitation," and product-liability claims for anything transmitted from the Web Site.
- **§8.e (p0055)** only gives an actual-knowledge non-infringement warranty on *Client Content*; nothing allocates IP risk in TrueLink's own technology to TrueLink.
- No indemnity procedure anywhere (notice, control of defense, settlement consent, cooperation).
- The §12 liability cap (p0077) is limited to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, so it does not undercut the new indemnity.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): added triggers (ii)–(v) to §12.b covering third-party IP infringement/misappropriation, TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content/Credit Data/Client Proprietary Information, and TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct; plus a new mutual §12.c indemnity procedure. The comment offers the fallback (customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies) if TrueLink resists the full scope.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 12.b gives us a TrueLink indemnity, but it is limited to TrueLink's breach of the Agreement or failure to perform. It contains no indemnity for third-party claims that the Interface or the hosted/support services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property, nor for TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content/Credit Data, or TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. By contrast, our indemnity in 12.a is very broad (any breach, all Web Site/Client Content claims expressly "without regard to any knowledge limitation," and product-liability claims for anything transmitted from the Web Site), and Section 8.e only gives an actual-knowledge non-infringement warranty on Client Content — so nothing shifts IP risk in TrueLink's own technology to TrueLink. The agreement also lacks any indemnity procedure (notice, control of defense, consent to settlement, cooperation). Per the detection guidance, a Vendor indemnity that excludes IP infringement is a deviation. We proposed adding the missing indemnity triggers to 12.b and a mutual indemnity procedure, with the customary-exclusions/remedies package available as a fallback.

Original paragraphs:
p0073: b. TrueLink shall indemnify and hold Client harmless, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to any
p0075: claim arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder.
p0071: a. Client shall indemnify and hold TrueLink, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to the following:
p0072: (i) any claim arising out of any breach by Client of this Agreement, (ii) any claim or demand resulting from any act or omission by Client or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client which constitutes a breach of or default by TrueLink under any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement, which breach or default has either not been cured or cannot be cured within the applicable cure period and the consequences of which is that TrueLink will lose material rights it has pursuant to said Agreements or a violation of any state or federal law, rule or regulation (iii) any claim arising out of or relating to the Web Site or Client Content (including, but not limited to, any claim resulting from any content posted to the Web Site by Client or Client's employees, agent or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client), without regard to any knowledge limitation or qualification that may be contained in this Agreement, and (iv) injury or damage to person or property caused by a product, service, or information, whether or not defective, that is sold, distributed or transmitted from the Web Site.

Resolved definitions:
Client: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.
TrueLink: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.

Rendered redline:
p0075: claim arising out of (i) any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder; (ii) any allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any other software, materials or deliverables provided by TrueLink infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right of any third party; (iii) any violation by TrueLink of any state or federal law, rule or regulation; (iv) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data or Client Proprietary Information caused by TrueLink; or (v) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
c. Indemnity Procedure. The party seeking indemnification shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim (provided that any delay in notice shall not relieve the indemnifying party except to the extent it is materially prejudiced), shall permit the indemnifying party to control the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or obligation on the indemnified party may be entered into without its prior written consent), and shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. The indemnified party may participate in the defense with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense.

Comment:
[Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity currently covers only its own breach of the Agreement, so we would carry the risk of third-party claims that the Interface or hosted services infringe IP rights, while our own indemnity is very broad. We added IP infringement, violation of law, TrueLink-caused data compromise and gross negligence/willful misconduct, plus a standard notice-and-control procedure; if TrueLink prefers, we can accept the IP indemnity with customary exclusions (our modifications, combinations and specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — LOL-CAP**

The agreement has no standalone limitation-of-liability section; the only cap sits at the end of Section 12 (Indemnity), at paragraph p0077, and it is one-sided:

- **One-way cap.** It limits only TrueLink's liability. Client (Mortgage Logic.com) is entirely uncapped, including under the very broad Section 12a indemnity — our walk-away position.
- **Weak basis.** "Total compensation **paid** for Hosting and Support Services" excludes amounts payable but unpaid and the "other services" fees contemplated by Section 5a, and there is no USD floor.
- **No mutual damages exclusion / carve-outs.** Only TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct are excepted; confidentiality (Section 10), indemnification, fraud and IP infringement are not carved out, and there is no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** replaced the single sentence in p0077 with a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and an "Excluded Claims" set (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification under Section 12, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) sitting outside the cap, with Client's fee payment obligations expressly not capped damages. Fallback offered in the comment: straight twelve months' fees with the carve-outs retained.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only liability cap in the agreement (buried at the end of Section 12, Indemnity) is one-sided: it limits TrueLink's liability alone, leaving Client's liability — including its very broad indemnity under Section 12a — entirely uncapped, which is our walk-away position. The cap basis is also narrow ("total compensation paid" for Hosting and Support Services only, excluding other agreed services under Section 5a and amounts payable but unpaid), and there is no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and no carve-out set beyond TrueLink's gross negligence/wilful misconduct. The redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and places indemnification, confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, with Client's payment obligations not treated as capped damages.

Original paragraphs:

Resolved definitions:

("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.

p0077: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CLIENT UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000, AND NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 12, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; CLIENT'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THE FOREGOING CAP.

Comment:
[Playbook] We made the limitation of liability mutual and meaningful — the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000 — rather than a one-way cap that protects only TrueLink while leaving Client's liability unlimited, and we added a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages. Consistent with our playbook, indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Client's obligation to pay fees is not capped; if helpful we can fall back to a straight twelve months' fees cap with these carve-outs retained.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.rationale: Section 13 (p0078) gives automatic successive one-year renewals with a 30-day non-renewal notice window, which already meets the preferred position on renewal term length and exit window. input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds Client anywhere in this Agreement, which matches our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline or comment is proposed and the fallback narrowing edits are correctly not applied. Reviewer note: the separate Non-Competition Agreement is outside this document and should be diligenced separately for any hiring restriction binding us.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The Agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us:

- **Text searches** for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "staff" surfaced only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), the access-restriction covenant in § 8(c), and incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities.
- **Full read of the two likely locations** flagged by the plan — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirms no hiring restriction is tucked into our covenants or the confidentiality obligations.
- **One cross-reference noted:** § 8(d) (p0054) refers to a separate "Non-Competition Agreement", but only to bound TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data — not personnel hiring. That instrument sits outside this document; if it is in the deal package, it is worth a separate check for a non-solicit binding us.

This is our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so we take no action rather than importing the mutual fallback.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: Section 12.b's TrueLink indemnity is limited to TrueLink's breach/non-performance and contains no IP infringement, violation-of-law, data-compromise or gross negligence/willful misconduct trigger, which the detection guidance expressly treats as a deviation even though a (broad) Customer indemnity exists in 12.a.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it adds the four preferred-position triggers to 12.b (IP infringement of the Interface/Hosting/Support Services, TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content/Credit Data, gross negligence/willful misconduct) and inserts a balanced notice/control/cooperation/no-adverse-settlement procedure, using the existing 'claim arising out of' sentence structure.

Deterministic flags are not disqualifying: the 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' regex misses a phrasing variant (the inserted limb plainly covers 'infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right'), and the 0.779 changed-character ratio on p0075 reflects the unavoidable expansion of a single-trigger sentence fragment into an enumerated list.
Comment is accurate, in-house voice, cites the playbook position and offers the sanctioned fallback (customary exclusions plus procure/modify/replace/refund).

Minor follow-ups, not grounds to fail: the proposal does not actually narrow Customer's 12.a indemnity (notably limb (iii)'s 'without regard to any knowledge limitation' and limb (iv)'s product-liability sweep), which the preferred position contemplates, and the new subsection should be confirmed as the next available letter in Section 12 and that 'Hosting Services'/'Support Services'/'Client Proprietary Information' are defined terms in the agreement.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (medium severity) — RENEWAL**

The renewal terms are buried in the mis-numbered Section 13 (paragraph p0078, rendered under the § 12 Indemnity heading rather than a term/renewal section, contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint).

What the document already does well:
- **Renewal term:** successive **one-year** periods — matches the preferred 12-month position.
- **Exit window:** either party may give non-renewal notice **30 days** prior to term end — already at the preferred ≤ 30 days, well inside the walk-away threshold.

What was missing:
- **No vendor renewal reminder** — the customer bears the full burden of tracking the renewal date.
- **No renewal price cap.** Section 6 (p0047) freezes Hosting Services costs only "for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement," so uplift at each renewal is entirely uncapped after year one. (The most-favoured-rate promise in the same sentence limits relative pricing but not absolute increases.)

Redline (validated, ok:true): inserted into p0078 a requirement that TrueLink notify Client of each upcoming renewal at least 60 days before term end, and a cap on renewal fees at the lesser of CPI over the preceding 12 months and 3%. Fallback of 5% offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 13 (p0078) gives automatic successive one-year renewals with a 30-day non-renewal notice window, which already meets the preferred position on renewal term length and exit window. However, the agreement lacks the two remaining preferred protections: a vendor reminder ahead of renewal and a cap on renewal price increases. Section 6 (p0047) freezes Hosting Services costs only for the first year, leaving renewal-term uplift uncapped. The redline adds a 60-day TrueLink renewal reminder and caps renewal fees at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with 5% available as a fallback.

This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. **Finding submitted: Compliant** — no redline, no comment.

Nothing substantive required repair, so this resubmission tightens the rationale while holding the same conclusion, which the verifier's own commentary endorsed on every substantive point:

- **No covenant binds us.** Literal and regex searches across the full document ("solicit", "solicitation", "no-hire", "poach", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel", "staff", "leave the employ") surface only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities, and the quoted § 8(c) access-restriction covenant.
- **Both candidate locations read in full** — § 8 (Client covenants) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirming the absence rather than inferring it.
- **§ 8(d) is not a hiring restraint.** Its cross-reference to the separate Non-Competition Agreement is scoped to limitations on TrueLink's Credit Data licence.

On the persistent "general-solicitation carve-out: failed" check: I have not chased it, because the only way to make it pass would be to draft a non-solicit into the Agreement and then carve it back — creating a restriction on our own hiring where none exists today. That would be a clear loss for us. The check is unsatisfiable by design when the clause is absent, and absence is the playbook's preferred outcome.

One item genuinely outside my reach: the standalone Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d) is not in this document set, so a non-solicit or no-hire living there would not be captured here and should be diligenced separately against this rule.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds Client anywhere in this Agreement, which matches our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline or comment is proposed and the fallback narrowing edits are correctly not applied. Literal and regex searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "no-hire", "poach", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel", "staff" and "leave the employ" return only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities, and § 8(c) as quoted, where "employees" appears solely in an access-restriction covenant and imposes no hiring restraint. reasons: The cited text (p0077) is genuinely a one-way cap protecting only TrueLink, leaving Client's liability (including its broad Section 12a indemnity) uncapped — squarely the rule's walk-away scenario, so 'deviation' is correctly claimed.

The redline reaches the preferred position: mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, plus the carve-out that Client's fee obligations are not capped damages.

The original carve-out for TrueLink's gross negligence/wilful misconduct is preserved (now mutual) within the Excluded Claims definition, and the ALL-CAPS formatting of the source paragraph is retained.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is explained by the rule itself: the cap basis, mutuality and carve-out sentence all had to be rewritten; the edit stays within the single existing sentence rather than restructuring the section.

Comment is accurate, correctly states the playbook position and the 12-months'-fees fallback with carve-outs retained. Minor note only: the edit drops the original narrowing to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, which incidentally extends the cap to TrueLink's other breaches — acceptable here because it matches the model language and is offset by the broad Excluded Claims, but worth flagging to the negotiator.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

paragraphs.text: 2. LICENSE.

a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such

software or services do not infringe upon any of TrueLink's Intellectual Property. Nothing in the foregoing sentence is meant to affect in any way Client's confidentiality obligations pursuant to Section 10 herein.
b. Scope. The license granted to Client pursuant to section 2(a) consists of the following rights:
i. Use and execution of the Interface on a compatible software platform (as such compatibility specifications may be issued by TrueLink from time to time); and
ii. Access to the Interface from multiple computer located at those sites listed on Exhibit "A." Client may amend Exhibit "A" by giving TrueLink written notice of the new sites.
c. Term. The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12.
d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
3. HOSTING SERVICES. TrueLink will provide the following services to Client (the "Hosting Services"):
a. Storage. ___ megabytes (MB) of disk space on TrueLink's servers will be used for storage of the Web Site and any data files associated with the Web Site.

b. Response Time. TrueLink agrees to use reasonable commercial efforts, consistent with efforts provided to its other Clients to ensure reasonable response times for users accessing the Web Site. Reasonable response times shall be measured as follows: at a mutually agreed to time Client will conduct three tests of the time that it takes to load the home page of the Web Site from an IBM compatible computer (with a 16550 UART chip and an Intel 80586 300 MHZ processor running Windows 98 or NT and Microsoft Internet Explorer (with the cache turned off) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem (the results of these tests will be reported to TrueLink upon completion); reasonable response times means that at all times the time it takes to load the home page of the Web Site using a properly configured IBM compatible computer (as set forth above) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem shall in no event exceed twice the average of the three test response times.

c. Bandwidth. ___ MB of monthly bandwidth (data transfer). In the event that the response time is not reasonable as determined under section 3.1 hereof, upon written notice from Client, TrueLink will, within a reasonable period of time, use reasonable commercial efforts to increase the bandwidth as necessary to make the response time reasonable.

d. Availability. The Web Site will be available Client's to Internet users approximately 24 hours a day, seven days a week, normal maintenance and unforeseen hardware or communications problems excepted. To minimize server downtime during peak usage periods,
TrueLink will take all reasonable actions to attempt to schedule routine maintenance between the hours of 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. pacific standard time.
e. Access. Client will have access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files in real time via the Interface.

f. Backups. TrueLink will backup the Interface and all data files associated with it at least once each day and will store the backup materials in a safe, secure location, suitable for magnetic media, and not at
the same location as TrueLink's server.
g. Internet Connection. TrueLink will maintain redundant connections to the Internet on diverse backbones.

h. Domain Names. TrueLink shall provide assistance to Client in securing one or more domain names, sub-domain names or URL's associated therewith; provided that prior to TrueLink providing such assistance, Client shall engage in an appropriate trademark search reasonably satisfactory to TrueLink in order to establish that no domain name proposed by Client shall infringe upon the trademark, service mark, name, or logo of any third party. TrueLink will not be responsible for, or have any liability in connection with, the operation of the Web Site with respect to online commercial transactions, or for the transmission accuracy or completeness of any data or information to or from the Web Site or through the Interface by Client or Client's customers.

i. Credit Bureau Information. TrueLink shall transmit such credit data to Client through the Interface as may be permitted under the Credit Repository Agreements and applicable law, each as in affect from time to tome, and in accordance with the certain Credit Bureau Agreement between TrueLink and Client dated of even date herewith. Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface. TrueLink makes no representation or warranty, and shall have no liability for the truth or completeness of any data so transmitted.

4. SUPPORT SERVICES. For a period of not less than ____ months, TrueLink will make available to Client the services of at least one programmer identified by TrueLink and reasonably acceptable to Client to provide such Support Services as Client may reasonably request to TrueLink in writing for purposes of permitting Client to use the Interface in accordance with the License granted under Section 2 hereof and the other terms and conditions of this Agreement.

This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.

WHEREAS, TrueLink is in the business of (i) developing and licensing interface software (the "Interface") to third parties; (ii) providing access to credit bureau information to third parties through the Interface; and (iii) providing certain technical support and programming customization services to users of the Interface substantially similar to those specifically enumerated herein (collectively "Support Services"); and

WHEREAS, TrueLink is licensed (or will be licensed) to provide access through the Interface to automated underwriting systems made available by certain third party investors or mortgage insurers (each such system is referred to hereafter as a "System", and all systems for which TrueLink is licensed to provide access are collectively referred to hereafter as the "Systems"); and

WHEREAS, TrueLink is willing to provide to Client and to certain of Client's correspondent broker customers access to the Interface and various Support Services, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Termination for convenience**

**What I found**

- The term provisions are located in the mis-numbered tail of § 12: **¶p0078 (13. TERM)** — one-year initial term auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal.
- **¶p0079 (14. TERMINATION)** contains the only Client exit: "Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide … until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides … notice of its election to terminate."

**Why it deviates**

1. It is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic, not an express convenience right, and the effective date can run up to ~60 days.
2. It is qualified by a "Section 4" that does not exist in the document (the outline skips 3, 4, 6, 9, 11), leaving the right subject to unknown conditions — and § 5(a)/§ 6 reference **minimum monthly fees** that could be asserted post-termination.
3. No refund of prepaid fees and no express bar on early-termination charges.

**Direction check:** Vendor has no mid-term convenience right — only 30-day non-renewal at the end of each annual term — so no vendor-side deletion was required. Because the committed term is 12 months (not multi-year), this is a drafting-quality deviation rather than a missing-behaviour finding.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level, ¶p0079):** Client may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice; TrueLink services continue to the effective date; refund of prepaid fees; no early-termination fee, penalty or minimum-fee obligation for periods after termination. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback.
