content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no audit right against us to constrain.

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against Mortgage Logic.com. I confirmed this by keyword search (audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises) and by full reads of the planner's candidate sections plus the license and confidentiality sections:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — fee provisions run in our favour: we get supporting documentation on request and a right to contest charges. No reciprocal TrueLink verification right.
- **§ 8 (Client Covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no inspection right.
- **§ 3(e)** — we hold real-time access to usage statistics and raw log files, so TrueLink has no need for a usage audit.

Two access-flavoured provisions were reviewed and are not audits: § 8(f) permits TrueLink to implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and § 9 requires us to give access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at its own cost. Neither is a verification right, and neither grants remote access to our systems (the walk-away trigger).

Because no audit right binds the Customer, there is nothing to limit on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access — the current position is stronger than the playbook's preferred outcome, so I proposed no redline. Worth noting for negotiation discipline: if TrueLink later seeks to add a usage-verification or compliance-audit right, we should hold to the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access) rather than accept an unqualified right.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding submitted: `missing` (INSURANCE), confidence 0.90**

**What I found:** The Agreement has no insurance provision at all — a full-text search for "insurance" returned zero results, and the section outline confirms no insurance heading exists among Sections 1–30.

**Why it matters here:**
- TrueLink is a hosting vendor that hosts our Web Site, operates the Interface, and transmits Client Content and consumer credit data — squarely within the playbook's "processes Customer Data" trigger.
- TrueLink's liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 is already capped at 12 months of hosting/support fees (p0077), and it gives a mutual indemnity in Section 12(b) — neither is backed by any coverage requirement.
- This falls close to the walk-away line (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data), so the preferred position is proportionate rather than aggressive.

**Redline (validated `ok:true`):** Inserted a new **Section 31 (Insurance)** immediately after Section 30 (Force Majeure), the last substantive miscellaneous provision and just ahead of the signature blocks:

- CGL: USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate
- Professional liability (E&O): USD 2,000,000
- Cyber liability: USD 5,000,000 (tied to TrueLink's processing of Client Content and consumer data)
- Workers' compensation as required by law
- Certificates of insurance on request; term plus one year

**Direction check:** The obligation runs against the counterparty only and imposes nothing on us. The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if the limits meet resistance.

**One item worth flagging for your review:** the survival clause (p0090) covers "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so a new Section 31 would sit outside it. I deliberately left that alone to keep the edit minimal, since the new clause carries its own express duration ("throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter"). If you would rather belt-and-braces it, extending that reference to "5 through 31" is a trivial follow-on edit.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no insurance provision anywhere (a search for "insurance" returns no results, and the section outline shows no insurance heading). TrueLink is a hosting/services vendor that hosts our Web Site, operates the Interface and transmits Client Content and consumer credit data, and its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 is capped at 12 months' hosting/support fees (p0077), so the mutual indemnity in Section 12(b) is unsupported by any coverage. Under the playbook this is a deviation requiring insertion of standard coverage. We inserted a new Section 31 immediately after Section 30 (Force Majeure), the last substantive miscellaneous provision, requiring CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber liability of USD 5M (TrueLink processes our data), workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request. The obligation binds the counterparty only, so it does not create any burden on us; the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment.

p0097: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink. However, to be excused from delay or failure to perform, TrueLink must act diligently to remedy the cause of the delay or failure.

TrueLink: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.

p0097: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

**Finding re-submitted: Compliant** (no redline, no comment — the correct output for this rule).

The verifier's substantive review agreed with the original conclusion; the only failure was the deterministic `audit frequency limited` regex, which cannot match because there is no audit clause in the document to constrain. I repaired the finding by tightening the evidence base rather than changing the status:

- **Widened the negative search** — added `examine`, `usage`, `review` and `access to` to the earlier sweep (audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises). Every `access` hit is Client-favourable or unrelated: definitional (§1), the license grant (§2(b)(ii)), our own restriction covenant (§8(c)), and indemnity references to customers we admit (§12).
- **Re-anchored the quote** on §3(e), which is the strongest affirmative evidence — we hold real-time usage statistics and raw log files, so TrueLink has no hook for a usage audit in the first place.
- **Addressed the false signal expressly** in the rationale, so the record explains why the check cannot pass and why that is a better-than-preferred outcome.

The key judgment worth being explicit about: satisfying the frequency/notice/cost regex would require **first conceding an audit right we do not currently owe**. Drafting in those parameters would be a net loss, so the correct action is silence plus a negotiation note — if TrueLink later proposes a verification right, we hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access.

One caveat on confidence (0.88 rather than higher): §§ 5-6 contain unfilled blanks (`$____ per month`) and reference Exhibits A and B, which are not in the extracted text. If those exhibits carry a reporting or verification mechanic, this rule would need re-running against them.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit, inspection or usage-verification right runs against the Client anywhere in this Agreement, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term to cap and no redline is warranted. Confirmed by keyword searches returning no hits for audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises, examine and review, and by full reads of the fee provisions (SS 5-6), Client covenants (S 8), the license grant (S 2) and confidentiality (S 10). Every information flow runs in our favour: S 3(e) gives Client real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files, and S 6 entitles Client to documentation supporting charges plus a right to contest them, so TrueLink has no contractual hook for a usage audit. The two Client-side access items are not audit rights: S 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and S 9 requires Client access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost, at Client's request. Neither grants remote or direct access to Customer systems, so the walk-away trigger is not present. The failed deterministic check for an audit-frequency limit is a false signal: the pattern cannot match because there is no audit clause to limit, and silence here is a better outcome for us than the preferred position. Inserting frequency, notice and cost parameters would require first conceding an audit right we do not currently owe, so we take no action and instead flag for negotiation discipline that if TrueLink later proposes a verification right we should hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent, and no direct access to Client systems.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes an open-ended minimum monthly fee on Client (our party) for both Hosting and Support Services, and Section 6 strips our documentation and dispute rights for those minimums, so the amounts (still blank) would be payable regardless of usage. Although the term is one year with an automatic renewal and Client has a convenience termination right in Section 14, the floor is a take-or-pay element that our playbook resists; the minimal fix is to delete the parenthetical floor and the related carve-outs so we pay only for services actually requested. Fallback (a floor limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up) is offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit

No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: This is a hosting agreement under which TrueLink holds our Client Content and borrower/loan data, but neither § 13 (Term) nor § 14 (Termination) obliges TrueLink to return that data or assist with migration on exit. § 13 only places the burden on us to arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, and § 10 contains no return-of-materials mechanic. We therefore inserted the playbook exit clause into § 14: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and deletion with written certification thereafter. Because §§ 5 through 30 survive termination under § 24, the inserted obligation will remain enforceable post-termination.

**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity) — no post-termination transition or data-return obligation.**

What I found:
- **§ 14 (Termination)** only addresses how long TrueLink keeps serving after our notice — nothing about giving our data back.
- **§ 13 (Term)** actually runs *against* us: it makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, with no reciprocal vendor migration duty.
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** has no return-of-materials mechanic, and a document-wide search for "return" / "Client Data" found nothing relevant — only a mailing reference.
- Material exposure: TrueLink hosts our Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and borrower and loan data (expressly deemed Client Proprietary Information under § 10(c)), so an exit with no return right is a real walk-away risk.

Redline inserted after § 14 (validated `ok:true`), tracking the preferred position: (a) up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates on request; (b) return of our data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within 30 days; (c) deletion thereafter with written certification.

Drafting note: I anchored the clause inside § 14 deliberately — § 24 provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination, so the new obligation survives without needing a separate survival amendment. I also mirrored the document's own defined terms (Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, Client Proprietary Information) rather than importing "Customer Data," which is undefined here. The comment offers the 90-day fallback.

input.rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against the Client anywhere in this Agreement, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access parameter to cap and no redline is warranted. Confirmed by keyword searches returning no hits for audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises, examine and review, and by full reads of the fee provisions (SS 5-6), Client covenants (S 8), the license grant (S 2) and confidentiality (S 10). Every information flow runs in our favour: S 3(e) gives Client real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files, and S 6 entitles Client to documentation supporting charges plus a right to contest them, so TrueLink has no contractual hook for a usage audit. The two Vendor-side access items are not audit rights: S 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and S 9 requires Client access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost, at Client's request. Neither grants remote or direct access to Customer systems, so the walk-away trigger is absent. The failed deterministic check for an audit-frequency limit is a false signal: the pattern cannot match because no audit clause exists to limit, and silence is more favourable to us than the preferred position. Inserting frequency, notice and cost parameters would require first conceding an audit right we do not currently owe, so we take no action. Retained as internal negotiation discipline rather than a raised issue: if TrueLink later proposes a verification right, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent, and no direct access to Client systems. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no audit right against us to constrain.

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against Mortgage Logic.com. I confirmed this by keyword search (audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises) and by full reads of the planner's candidate sections plus the license and confidentiality sections:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — fee provisions run in our favour: we get supporting documentation on request and a right to contest charges. No reciprocal TrueLink verification right.
- **§ 8 (Client Covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no inspection right.
- **§ 3(e)** — we hold real-time access to usage statistics and raw log files, so TrueLink has no need for a usage audit.

Two access-flavoured provisions were reviewed and are not audits: § 8(f) permits TrueLink to implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and § 9 requires us to give access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at its own cost. Neither is a verification right, and neither grants remote access to our systems (the walk-away trigger).

Because no audit right binds the Customer, there is nothing to limit on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access — the current position is stronger than the playbook's preferred outcome, so I proposed no redline. Worth noting for negotiation discipline: if TrueLink later seeks to add a usage-verification or compliance-audit right, we should hold to the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access) rather than accept an unqualified right.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against the Client anywhere in this Agreement, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access parameter to cap and no redline is warranted. Confirmed by keyword searches returning no hits for audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises, examine and review, and by full reads of the fee provisions (SS 5-6), Client covenants (S 8), the license grant (S 2) and confidentiality (S 10). Every information flow runs in our favour: S 3(e) gives Client real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files, and S 6 entitles Client to documentation supporting charges plus a right to contest them, so TrueLink has no contractual hook for a usage audit. The two Vendor-side access items are not audit rights: S 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and S 9 requires Client access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost, at Client's request. Neither grants remote or direct access to Customer systems, so the walk-away trigger is absent. The failed deterministic check for an audit-frequency limit is a false signal: the pattern cannot match because no audit clause exists to limit, and silence is more favourable to us than the preferred position. Inserting frequency, notice and cost parameters would require first conceding an audit right we do not currently owe, so we take no action. Retained as internal negotiation discipline rather than a raised issue: if TrueLink later proposes a verification right, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent, and no direct access to Client systems. Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-3c735457","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 12.b gives us a TrueLink indemnity, but it is limited to TrueLink's breach of the Agreement or failure to perform. It contains no indemnity for third-party claims that the Interface or the hosted/support services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property, nor for TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content/Credit Data, or TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. By contrast, our indemnity in 12.a is very broad (any breach, all Web Site/Client Content claims expressly \"without regard to any knowledge limitation,\" and product-liability claims for anything transmitted from the Web Site), and Section 8.e only gives an actual-knowledge non-infringement warranty on Client Content — so nothing shifts IP risk in TrueLink's own technology to TrueLink. The agreement also lacks any indemnity procedure (notice, control of defense, consent to settlement, cooperation). Per the detection guidance, a Vendor indemnity that excludes IP infringement is a deviation. We proposed adding the missing indemnity triggers to 12.b and a mutual indemnity procedure, with the customary-exclusions/remedies package available as a fallback.","proposal":"Expand TrueLink's indemnity in Section 12.b to cover third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Interface and services, TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client data, and TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and add a standard indemnity procedure.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-168fb636","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The only ownership provision (§2(d)) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface; nothing in the Agreement confirms that we own Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, our borrower/loan data or the results of the Support Services (deliverables), which TrueLink's programmer creates for us. Section 10 only treats those items as Client Proprietary Information for confidentiality purposes, which is not an ownership right, and §8(d) grants TrueLink a broad licence (use, resell, exploit) over Credit Data without any statement that we retain title. This is a critical gap under the IP rule, so we insert a reciprocal Client ownership clause with assignment of deliverables, a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, and no joint ownership. The cap basis is also narrow (\"total compensation paid\" for Hosting and Support Services only, excluding other agreed services under Section 5a and amounts payable but unpaid), and there is no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and no carve-out set beyond TrueLink's gross negligence/wilful misconduct. The redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and places indemnification, confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, with Client's payment obligations not treated as capped damages.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual, set it at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is a symmetrical consent-based prohibition. It gives Client only a limited \"financially responsible affiliate\" carve-out with no successor/M&A carve-out, so a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Client's assets would require TrueLink's consent, and the consent standard is unqualified (TrueLink could withhold arbitrarily). Conversely, TrueLink's assignment is not barred from going to a Client competitor. There is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement (no \"change of control\" language appears), so no walk-away issue, but the clause falls short of the preferred position and is a high-severity assignment deviation. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, a reasonableness standard on Client's consent to TrueLink assignments, a no-competitor restriction, and confirms a Client change of control triggers no vendor right.","proposal":"Add Client affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, reasonableness standard on Client consent, no assignment to a Client competitor, and no vendor right arising from Client change of control.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-598142d0","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"Section 3(i) imposes a requirements-style sourcing obligation on us: we must order the credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no category/time limit and no exit for TrueLink's performance failures. Although the license in Section 2(a) is non-exclusive and expressly preserves our right to use alternative systems, that carve-out does not displace this mandatory per-borrower purchase obligation. The playbook preferred position is no sole-supplier obligation on the customer, so we make the order optional and confirm non-exclusivity; the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, terminable on service-level failure) is offered in the comment. The nonexclusive licenses granted to TrueLink in Section 8(d) are not exclusivity against us and are not flagged.","proposal":"Make credit report ordering optional so Client is not required to source all Interface-related credit reports from TrueLink.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-0b884700","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"No liquidated damages, penalties, or stipulated-sum charges payable by Client appear anywhere in the Agreement. The only Client-payable amounts are ordinary fees under § 5(a), including uncontestable minimum monthly fees, which are consideration for services actually delivered rather than damages. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface and Support Services Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review findings and negotiation positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is materially one-sided in TrueLink's favour on risk allocation: the only liability cap limits TrueLink alone and leaves our liability — including a very broad Client indemnity — entirely uncapped, which is a walk-away position for us. TrueLink's indemnity is narrow (breach/failure to perform only) with no IP infringement, violation of law, unauthorised access, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, and no indemnity procedure. The Agreement also never confirms that we own Client Content, our borrower/loan data or the Support Services deliverables, even though TrueLink's programmer creates those deliverables for us and TrueLink takes a broad Credit Data licence under § 8(d).

Several operational protections are simply absent: no post-termination data return or transition assistance in a hosting deal where TrueLink holds our data; no performance warranty beyond a Year 2000 warranty; and no insurance requirement at all. On the commercial side, § 3(i) imposes a requirements-style obligation to order every credit report from TrueLink, § 5(a) imposes an open-ended (and still blank) minimum monthly fee, renewal pricing is uncapped after year one, and § 14 is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic rather than a clean convenience right.

Some items are favourable and require no action: no non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds us (§ 2(a) expressly preserves our right to use competing systems), no MFN burdens us (the pricing-parity undertaking runs in our favour), no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us, and governing law/venue (California; San Luis Obispo County courts, no arbitration) sits within our accepted list.

Two findings did not pass automated verification and are recorded as **needs review** — audit rights and employee non-solicitation. In both cases the deterministic checks failed only because no such clause exists to measure; silence is more favourable to us than our preferred position, and no redline is proposed. Reviewer confirmation is nonetheless recommended.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Issue | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Cap is one-sided (TrueLink only); our liability, including the broad § 12a indemnity, is uncapped. Narrow cap basis, no mutual consequential-damages exclusion, no carve-out set. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | § 12.b covers only TrueLink's breach/failure to perform: no IP infringement, violation of law, unauthorised access to Client Content/Credit Data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; no indemnity procedure. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | No Client ownership provision; § 2(d) confirms only TrueLink's rights. Confidentiality treatment under § 10 is not ownership; § 8(d) grants a broad Credit Data licence with no retained-title statement. | Missing | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | § 3(i) requires us to order the credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no category/time limit and no exit for performance failure. | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Grant runs to Client only (no affiliates/contractors); § 13(b) cuts off §§ 2–3 for "any violations or breach" of §§ 8a–8c with no materiality threshold or cure period; no successor transfer. | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 6 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | § 15 consent regime gives us only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out, unqualified consent standard, and no bar on assignment to our competitor. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | No liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; § 5(a) amounts are fees for services, and § 14 carries no early-termination fee. | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us; § 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or use competing software and services. | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 9 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | § 9 warrants only Year 2000 date processing: no professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy. | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| 10 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | No obligation on TrueLink to return our data or assist migration; §§ 13–14 place the burden on us (new name server in 30 days, new hosting in 60 days). | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | § 5(a) imposes an open-ended (still blank) minimum monthly fee for Hosting and Support Services; § 6 strips our documentation and dispute rights for those minimums. | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 12 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | § 14 is a service-continuation mechanic, cross-references a non-existent "Section 4", allows up to ~60 days to effectiveness, and provides no refund of prepaid fees or bar on minimum-fee charges. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Renewal term and 30-day exit window are acceptable, but there is no vendor renewal reminder and no cap on renewal price increases (§ 6 freezes Hosting costs for year one only). | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | California law (§ 26); exclusive state/federal courts in San Luis Obispo County (§ 27); no arbitration. Within our accepted list. | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | No MFN burdens us; TrueLink undertakes that Hosting Services rates will not exceed those charged to any other party, plus a one-year price freeze. | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 16 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right runs against us; information flows favour us (§ 3(e) usage statistics and logs; § 6 supporting documentation and right to contest). No redline. *Automated check did not verify — reviewer confirmation recommended.* | Needs review | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds us; "employees" appears only in the § 12 indemnities and the § 8(c) access-restriction covenant. No redline. *Automated check did not verify — reviewer confirmation recommended.* | Needs review | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | No insurance provision anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and transmitting Client Content and consumer credit data. | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Client liability (LOL-CAP, § 12).** Our playbook treats a cap that protects the vendor alone while leaving our liability — including the very broad § 12a indemnity — uncapped as a walk-away position. We require a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, and carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with our payment obligations not treated as capped damages.

*Note on the assignment finding:* although § 15 falls short of our preferred position, there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement, so this is a high-severity deviation rather than a walk-away item.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Table the ri[REDACTED] package as a single negotiation.** Present the mutual cap (item 1), the expanded § 12.b indemnity triggers plus a mutual indemnity procedure (item 2), and the Client ownership/assignment-of-deliverables clause with a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP (item 3) together. On the indemnity, the customary-exclusions/remedies package is available as our fallback. We leave the negotiated § 8(d) Credit Data licence intact, clarifying only that it is a licence and not a transfer of ownership.
2. **Press the commercial deviations.** Make credit report ordering optional (fallback: category-limited, 12 months, terminable on service-level failure); delete the § 5(a) minimum monthly fee floor (fallback: floor limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up); extend the licence to affiliates and contractors, add successor transfer and limit the § 13(b) cut-off to uncured material breach; and add the affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, a reasonableness standard on our consent to TrueLink assignments, a no-competitor restriction, and confirmation that our change of control triggers no vendor right.
3. **Close the operational gaps.** Insert into § 14 up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable format within thirty days, and deletion with written certification (enforceable post-termination, as §§ 5–30 survive under § 24); add the performance warranty and remedy to § 9; add a 60-day renewal reminder and cap renewal fees at the lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%); conform § 14 to an express convenience right on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees and no penalty; and add the new insurance section (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
4. **Resolve open drafting and diligence points.** (a) §§ 5–6 contain unfilled fee blanks and reference Exhibits A and B, which were not in the extracted text — obtain them and re-run the audit rule against them in case they carry a reporting or verification mechanic. (b) The separate "Non-Competition Agreement" referenced at § 8(d) is not defined here and sits outside this document; diligence it separately for any restriction binding us, including any hiring restriction. (c) § 14's cross-reference to "Section 4" does not correspond to any section in the Agreement and should be corrected.
5. **Hold internal discipline on audit.** No audit right currently runs against us and we are not conceding one. If TrueLink later proposes a verification right, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems."}
